Reproducing Lefebvre et al. (2008), Figure 9, from CRCNS ret-1¶

Paper. Lefebvre JL, Zhang Y, Meister M, Wang X, Sanes JR (2008). Gamma-Protocadherins regulate neuronal survival but are dispensable for circuit formation in retina. Development 135:4141-4151. doi:10.1242/dev.027912. The claims file was written from the NIH author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC2644426), with its Methods, Results, Discussion and figure legends; the supplementary figures were not available to it. The paper links no analysis code.

Data set. CRCNS ret-1, "Multi-electrode recordings from retinal ganglion cells" (Zhang, Asari and Meister 2014), doi:10.6080/K0RF5RZT, read from the public S3 bucket crcnsarchive under ret-1/. CRCNS data sets are not versioned, so the version is recorded as unversioned. There is one form of the data set to choose: the paper (2008) predates it and cites none, and the bucket holds one zip file, crcns_ret-1.zip (71,871,914 bytes), whose MD5 in the data set's checksums.md5 is 4b9390ddc51c72d6f66563cb02e48fe8; the data check below streams the zip and confirms that sum, and lists the CRC-32 of every member read, so that a later change is detectable. The description is version 0.8 (2 September 2014) and the files in the zip are dated 2014. The zip is opened in place over range requests; nothing is written to disk.

What the data set holds. Spike times of 325 sorted units from 16 isolated retinas (5 dates in 2008), each file labelled with a genotype, and their responses to binary white noise only: flickering vertical and horizontal bars and checkerboards, drawn from the RAN1 generator whose bits are in the zip. It holds none of the histology of Figures 1 to 8, and none of the flashing spots, flashes, moving bars or gratings of Figure 9A to 9C.

Outside inputs. None.

Claim Tested here
fig1-broad-expression, fig2-postnatal-localization, fig3-synaptic-localization, s1-chx10-recombination, fig4h-inl-ipl-thinner, fig4-alleles-equivalent, fig4i-cell-type-loss, fig5-postnatal-onset, fig5-increased-apoptosis, fig6f-amacrine-loss-central, fig6f-neighbours, fig7-laminar-targeting, fig8ad-bax-rescue, fig8el-synapse-density, fig8mn-bax-laminar Blocked: histology, not in the data set

Which bar recording. The paper names bars of 8.3 or 16.6 um but not their orientation, nor what is done when a retina has more than one such recording. This was asked (questions/crcns-ret-1.yaml); the reader found that the paper does not say, and the claims file now names three readings in the criterion of fig9d-rf-size-similar and requires every claim on the bars to be judged under all three: (A) the first vertical-bar recording of each retina at 8.3 or 16.6 um, (B) all its vertical-bar recordings at those widths pooled, spikes and frames together, (C) its horizontal-bar recording where it has one, otherwise as A.

with requests.get(ret1.BASE_URL + ret1.ZIP_NAME, stream=True, timeout=120) as r:

print("\nMembers read (size in bytes and CRC-32 from the zip directory):")
for info in z.infolist():
    if info.filename.startswith(ret1.PREFIX) and not info.is_dir():
        print(f"  {info.filename:40s} {info.file_size:>10,d}  {info.CRC:08x}")

The 16 files match the description's table in cell counts and genotype labels. Every recording is binary white noise drawn from RAN1 with seed -10000: vertical bars (full height), horizontal bars (full width) or checkerboards. There are no flashing spots, flashes of different intensity, moving bars or drifting gratings, so the stimuli of Figure 9A, 9B and 9C and of the rod and cone test are not in the data set. The pixel size is 8.3 um as stated, so the bars are 8.3, 16.6 and (one recording) 41.5 um wide, the widths the Methods give except the last. Frames last 16.67 ms (60 Hz) for the bars, as the Methods state, and 33.3 ms for some checkerboards; two recordings of 20080702 state 16.665 and 16.669 ms.

The labels give 200 mutant cells in 10 retinas (Chx10-Cre 87, Pax6-Cre 113), 3 cells from one Bax -/- mutant retina, and 122 control cells in 5 retinas, 95 of them labelled "chx10 het". The paper's Figure 9 has 115 mutant and 143 control cells, and names its controls Pax6-Cre; Pcdh-gamma +/f-del or Pcdh-gamma f-del/f-del without Cre; it names no Chx10-Cre heterozygous controls. The files do not say which part of the Pax6-Cre retinas was recorded (the paper used their peripheral region only), nor the age of the mice, nor the allele.

# ran1.bin against the RAN1 generator of ran1.m, and the bit order.
check = ret1.ran1(-10000, 20000) >= 0.5
with z.open(ret1.PREFIX + "ran1.bin") as f:
    raw = np.frombuffer(f.read(2500), dtype=np.uint8)
for order in ("little", "big"):
    agree = (np.unpackbits(raw, bitorder=order)[:20000].astype(bool) == check).mean()
    print(f"first 20000 bits, {order}-endian bit order: {agree:.4f} agree with RAN1(seed -10000) >= 0.5")
print("ran1.bin holds", z.getinfo(ret1.PREFIX + "ran1.bin").file_size * 8, "bits; the longest stimulus needs", nbits)

# Spike times: units, order, and range against the stimulus window.
rows = []
for R in retinas:
    for rec in R["recordings"]:
        end = rec["onset"] + rec["nframes"] * rec["frame"]
        parts = ret1.split_trains(rec)
        tails = [tl for _, tl in parts if len(tl)]
        allt = np.concatenate([t for t in rec["spikes"] if len(t)])
        rows.append({"retina": R["retina"], "rec": rec["index"], "kind": ret1.kind(rec), "onset_s": round(rec["onset"], 2),
                     "stim_end_s": round(end, 1), "first_spike_s": round(allt.min(), 3), "last_spike_s": round(allt.max(), 1),
                     "spikes_after_end": int((allt > end).sum()),
                     "unsorted_trains": len(tails), "head_ends_s": round(max((h.max() for h, tl in parts if len(tl)), default=np.nan), 1),
                     "tail_span_s": (f"{min(t.min() for t in tails):.1f}-{max(t.max() for t in tails):.1f}" if tails else ""),
                     "tail_spikes": int(sum(len(t) for t in tails))})
spk = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(spk.to_string(index=False))
print("\nRecordings with out-of-order spike times:", int((spk.unsorted_trains > 0).sum()), "of", len(spk),
      "; trains affected:", int(spk.unsorted_trains.sum()), "; spikes in the out-of-order segments:", int(spk.tail_spikes.sum()))

# Where do the out-of-order segments belong? STA of the tail spikes alone, at their stored times and
# moved by 720 s (to 1440-1500 s, the part of the recording that has no spikes otherwise).
def peak_ratios(rec, trains, nlag=15):
    r = dict(rec); r["spikes"] = trains
    S, C = ret1.stimulus(r, bits), ret1.counts(r)
    h, n = ret1.sta(S, C, nlag)
    hn, _ = ret1.sta(S, np.roll(C, C.shape[0] // 2, axis=0), nlag)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
        return np.abs(h).reshape(len(n), -1).max(1) / np.abs(hn).reshape(len(n), -1).max(1), n

tail_rows = []
for R in retinas:
    rec = R["recordings"][0]
    parts = ret1.split_trains(rec)
    if ret1.kind(rec) == "checker" or not any(len(tl) for _, tl in parts):
        continue
    stored, n = peak_ratios(rec, [tl for _, tl in parts])
    moved, _ = peak_ratios(rec, [tl + 720.0 for _, tl in parts])
    ok = n >= 50
    tail_rows.append({"retina": R["retina"], "rec": rec["index"], "cells_with_50_tail_spikes": int(ok.sum()),
                      "median_ratio_stored": round(float(np.median(stored[ok])), 2), "median_ratio_moved_720s": round(float(np.median(moved[ok])), 2),
                      "cells_higher_when_moved": int((moved[ok] > stored[ok]).sum())})
print(pd.DataFrame(tail_rows).to_string(index=False))
print("\nTrains without an out-of-order segment in the same recordings: spikes in 1440-1500 s and in 720-780 s")
for R in retinas:
    for rec in R["recordings"]:
        parts = ret1.split_trains(rec)
        if any(len(tl) for _, tl in parts) and rec["nframes"] * rec["frame"] > 1450:
            for c, (h, tl) in enumerate(parts):
                if not len(tl):
                    print(f"  {R['retina']} rec {rec['index']} unit {c}: {int((h > 1440).sum())} and {int(((h > 720) & (h < 780)).sum())}")

Spike times are in seconds from the start of each recording and begin before the stimulus onset (about 1 s), as the example script assumes. In the 8 recordings of 20080628_R4 and R6 and of 20080702_R1 and R4 (vertical bars and checkerboards, each of 1500 s), almost every train is out of order: it runs from 0 to 1440 s and then holds a second segment of spikes between 720 and 780 s, though the stimulus runs to 1500 s. The few trains in these recordings that are in order have spikes between 1440 and 1500 s, about as many as between 720 and 780 s (list above). Moved by 720 s, to 1440 to 1500 s, these segments give higher STA peaks over the null than where they are stored, in most cells of the larger retinas (table above). The segments are consistent with the last minute of each recording stored with the wrong offset, but this is not proven. The main analysis uses the spike times as deposited; a variant moves the segments. (One checkerboard recording, 20080628_R5, has 1 or 2 spikes near 2 s out of order in several cells; it is not used.)

No recording is deposited twice: no spike train repeats across files or units. Within recordings, the pairs above share 70 to 100% of their spikes within 0.5 ms in every recording of the retina, so each pair is most likely one neuron sorted twice. All units are kept in the main analysis, as the claims count all units; a variant drops the second unit of each pair.

# Clock: does the stimulus, rebuilt from its onset and frame length, line up with the spikes? Per
# recording, the STA peak over that of a null STA (spike counts circularly shifted by half the
# recording), and the lag of the STA peak. A response aligned to the stimulus gives ratios well
# above 1 at a consistent lag; misaligned timing gives ratios near 1.
clock = []
for R in retinas:
    for rec in R["recordings"]:
        if ret1.kind(rec) == "checker" and R["retina"] not in ("20080702_R4", "20080702_R1", "20080606_R1", "20080606_R2", "20080606_R3"):
            continue
        ratio, n = peak_ratios(rec, rec["spikes"], nlag=ret1.STA_FRAMES)
        S, C = ret1.stimulus(rec, bits), ret1.counts(rec)
        h, _ = ret1.sta(S, C)
        lag_ms = np.array([(np.unravel_index(np.nanargmax(np.abs(x)), x.shape)[1] + 0.5) * rec["frame"] * 1000 if n[i] else np.nan
                           for i, x in enumerate(h)])
        clock.append({"retina": R["retina"], "group": ret1.group(R["animal"]), "rec": rec["index"], "kind": ret1.kind(rec),
                      "cells": len(n), "median_ratio": round(float(np.nanmedian(ratio)), 2), "cells_ratio_above_2": int((ratio > 2).sum()),
                      "median_peak_lag_ms": round(float(np.nanmedian(lag_ms)), 0)})
clock = pd.DataFrame(clock)
print(clock.to_string(index=False))

For most bar recordings the STA peaks lie well above the null at lags of about 100 to 140 ms, so the stimulus as rebuilt shares the clock of the spikes. The vertical bars of 20080702_R4 are the exception: with the stated frame none of its 12 cells has an STA above the null (median ratio about 1), while the same cells give clear STAs to the checkerboard of the same retina. The search below shows why.

In [9]:
# Alignment search. (1) The frame length: the two vertical-bar recordings of 20080702 state 16.665
# and 16.669 ms, where every other bar recording states 16.672 ms; scan it in steps of 0.001 ms.
# (2) The onset: STAs at lags from -2 s to +2.5 s (moving the onset by k frames moves the window of
# lags by k), for the weak 20080606 retinas and 20080702_R4. Per lag, the median over cells of the
# STA's largest |value| at that lag over the null's peak; an aligned recording peaks at 100 to 140 ms.
bar_frames = pd.Series({(R["retina"], rec["index"]): rec["frame"] for R in retinas for rec in R["recordings"] if ret1.kind(rec) != "checker"})
common = float(bar_frames.median())
off = bar_frames[(bar_frames - common).abs() > 1e-6]
print(f"Stated frame of the {len(bar_frames)} bar recordings: median {common * 1000:.4f} ms; "
      f"{len(bar_frames) - len(off)} within 0.001 ms of it; the others: {(off * 1000).round(4).to_dict()}")
print("Checkerboard frames of 20080702, halved (ms):",
      {R["retina"]: round(r["frame"] / 2 * 1000, 4) for R in retinas if R["retina"].startswith("20080702") for r in R["recordings"] if ret1.kind(r) == "checker"})


def lag_profile(rec, frame, lags, nlag=ret1.STA_FRAMES):
    """Per lag, the median over cells of max |STA| over bars at that lag, over the null STA's peak."""
    r = dict(rec); r["frame"] = frame
    S, C = ret1.stimulus(r, bits), ret1.counts(r)
    a = np.abs(ret1.wide_sta(S, C, lags)).max(axis=1)
    hn = ret1.wide_sta(S, np.roll(C, C.shape[0] // 2, axis=0), np.arange(nlag))
    pn = np.abs(hn).reshape(len(hn), -1).max(axis=1)
    return np.median(a / pn[:, None], axis=0), a / pn[:, None]


scan = []
for (name, i), fr in off.items():
    rec = by_name[name]["recordings"][i]
    for f in [fr] + list(np.arange(16.664, 16.6765, 0.001) / 1000) + [common]:
        _, a = lag_profile(rec, f, np.arange(ret1.STA_FRAMES))
        scan.append({"retina": name, "rec": i, "frame_ms": round(f * 1000, 4), "stated": f == fr, "common": f == common,
                     "median_peak_ratio": round(float(np.median(a.max(axis=1))), 2), "cells_ratio_above_2": int((a.max(axis=1) > 2).sum()), "cells": len(a)})
scan = pd.DataFrame(scan)
print("\nFrame scan, onset as stated:"); print(scan.to_string(index=False))

lags = np.arange(-120, 150)
onset = []
for name in ("20080606_R1", "20080606_R2", "20080606_R3", "20080702_R4"):
    for rec in by_name[name]["recordings"]:
        for label, f in (("stated", rec["frame"]), ("common", common)):
            if label == "common" and (ret1.kind(rec) == "checker" or abs(rec["frame"] - common) < 1e-6):
                continue
            prof, _ = lag_profile(rec, f, lags)
            k = int(np.argmax(prof))
            far = prof[np.abs(lags - lags[k]) > 30]
            onset.append({"retina": name, "rec": rec["index"], "kind": ret1.kind(rec), "frame": label, "cells": by_name[name]["ncell"],
                          "peak_lag_ms": round((lags[k] + 0.5) * f * 1000), "profile_at_peak": round(float(prof[k]), 2),
                          "max_beyond_0.5s_of_peak": round(float(far.max()), 2), "median_over_lags": round(float(np.median(prof)), 2)})
print("\nOnset search, lags -2 to +2.5 s:"); print(pd.DataFrame(onset).to_string(index=False))

The stated frames of the two 20080702 vertical-bar recordings (16.6653 and 16.6691 ms) are not those of the stimulus. Over about 90,000 frames, a frame 0.0065 ms too short drifts by about 0.6 s, which smears the STA. The scan peaks at 16.671 to 16.672 ms in both recordings (20080702_R4: median ratio 2.79 and 2.76, against 0.96 at the stated frame; 20080702_R1: 3.54 and 4.16, against 2.27). That is the frame of the other 22 bar recordings (median 16.6718 ms), and half the checkerboard frame of the same two retinas. The data are trusted over the description: from here on these two recordings use 16.6718 ms, and a variant keeps the stated frames. With it, the lag profile of 20080702_R4 peaks at 158 ms; with the stated frame it has no peak (its largest value, 1.11, is at 775 ms).

The onset search finds no better alignment for the 20080606 retinas (all mutant). In every bar and checkerboard recording of 20080606_R1 and R2 the profile peaks at 125 to 175 ms, above its largest value more than 0.5 s from the peak. The single cell of 20080606_R3 has no clear peak in its bar recordings (largest value 1.38 at -1242 ms in the vertical bars, against 1.31 within the stated window), but its checkerboard profile peaks at 158 ms. So the weak STAs of these retinas are weak responses at the stated onset, not a misalignment that a shift of up to 2 s would repair.

GROUPS = ("mutant", "control")
CI = ("binomial", "dkw", "bootstrap")


def split(df, col):
    return df[df.group == "mutant"][col].to_numpy(float), df[df.group == "control"][col].to_numpy(float)


def judge(df, cols, rng, label=None):
    """For each measure column and CI reading: medians, KS test, and whether the 95% bands separate."""
    out = []
    for col in cols:
        m, c = split(df, col)
        m, c = m[np.isfinite(m)], c[np.isfinite(c)]
        ks = stats.ks_2samp(m, c)
        for ci in CI:
            r = ret1.compare_bands(m, c, ci, rng)
            out.append({**({"variant": label} if label else {}), "measure": col, "ci": ci, "n_mut": r["n_mutant"], "n_ctl": r["n_control"],
                        "median_mut": np.median(m), "median_ctl": np.median(c), "ks_p": ks.pvalue,
                        "separate": r["separate"], "mutant_larger_pts": r["mutant_right"], "mutant_smaller_pts": r["mutant_left"],
                        "sep_range": (f"{r['range'][0]:.3g} to {r['range'][1]:.3g}" if r["range"] else "")})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


def by_retina(df, cols):
    return df[df.group.isin(GROUPS)].groupby(["group", "retina"])[cols].agg(["median", "size"]).round(3)


def variants(rng, cols):
    """The same comparison, reading A, on subsets and on the corrected spike times."""
    A = cells[cells.reading == "A"]
    sets = {
        "all units (main)": A,
        "without duplicate units": A[~A.duplicate],
        "without 20080702_R4": A[A.retina != "20080702_R4"],
        "out-of-order segments moved 720 s": cells[cells.reading == "A, segments moved"],
        "20080702 frames as deposited": cells[cells.reading == "A, frames as deposited"],
        "mutant Chx10-Cre only": A[(A.group == "control") | A.animal.str.contains("chx10") & (A.group == "mutant")],
        "mutant Pax6-Cre only": A[(A.group == "control") | A.animal.str.contains("pax6") & (A.group == "mutant")],
        "control Pax6-Cre het only": A[(A.group == "mutant") | (A.animal == "WT (pax6 het)")],
        "cells with STA peak ratio above 2": A[A.peak_ratio > 2],
        "16.6 um bars only": A[A.bar_um == 16.6],
    }
    return pd.concat([judge(d[d.group.isin(GROUPS)], cols, rng, label=k) for k, d in sets.items()], ignore_index=True)


def ecdf_plot(ax, df, col, title, xlabel, scale=1.0):
    for g, colour in (("mutant", "tab:red"), ("control", "black")):
        v = np.sort(df[df.group == g][col].dropna().to_numpy() * scale)
        ax.step(v, np.arange(1, len(v) + 1) / len(v), where="post", color=colour, label=f"{g} ({len(v)})")
        lo, hi = ret1.band(v, v, "binomial")
        ax.fill_between(v, lo, hi, step="post", color=colour, alpha=0.15)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=9); ax.set_xlabel(xlabel); ax.set_ylabel("cumulative fraction"); ax.legend(fontsize=8)


def separating_points(m, c, ci, rng):
    """Every value where the two bands separate: the cells at or below it in each group and the bands."""
    m, c = m[np.isfinite(m)], c[np.isfinite(c)]
    grid = np.unique(np.concatenate([m, c]))
    lm, hm = ret1.band(m, grid, ci, rng)
    lc, hc = ret1.band(c, grid, ci, rng)
    sep = (hm < lc) | (hc < lm)
    return pd.DataFrame({"value": grid[sep], "mutant_at_or_below": np.searchsorted(np.sort(m), grid[sep], "right"), "n_mut": len(m),
                         "control_at_or_below": np.searchsorted(np.sort(c), grid[sep], "right"), "n_ctl": len(c),
                         "mutant_band": [f"{a:.3f}-{b:.3f}" for a, b in zip(lm[sep], hm[sep])],
                         "control_band": [f"{a:.3f}-{b:.3f}" for a, b in zip(lc[sep], hc[sep])],
                         "direction": np.where(hm[sep] < lc[sep], "mutant larger", "mutant smaller")})

The bands under shuffled labels¶

How often do the bands separate when the groups do not differ? For the main measures of the claims (reading A), the group labels are shuffled over the 322 cells, keeping the group sizes, 200 times, and the bands compared as in the claims. This is the rate at which "the bands separate" is met by chance under each band reading, with these cells' values.

             "gain_frame_printed", "gain_frame_continuous"]
NSHUF = 200
t0 = time.time()
rows = []
for col in null_cols:
    x = A[col].to_numpy(float)
    is_mut = (A.group == "mutant").to_numpy()
    for ci in CI:
        sep = 0
        for _ in range(NSHUF):
            lab = rng.permutation(is_mut)
            sep += ret1.compare_bands(x[lab], x[~lab], ci, rng)["separate"]
        rows.append({"measure": col, "ci": ci, "shuffles": NSHUF, "separate": sep, "rate": sep / NSHUF})
null_rates = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(null_rates.pivot(index="measure", columns="ci", values="rate").round(3).to_string())
print(f"\nRate over all measures: {null_rates.groupby('ci').separate.sum().div(null_rates.groupby('ci').shuffles.sum()).round(3).to_dict()}"
      f"; {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

Under shuffled labels the binomial bands separate in 26 to 43% of shuffles, depending on the measure (35% over all), the bootstrap bands in 26 to 45% (37%), and the DKW bands in none of 1600. Both pointwise bands have zero width where a group's cumulative fraction is 0 or 1, so a few cells beyond the other group's range are enough to separate them. A separation under the binomial or bootstrap band alone is therefore weak evidence of a difference, and an overlap under every band reading, which the claims of absence require, fails for about a third of pairs of samples drawn from one distribution. The criteria are the claims file's and are applied as written; each conclusion below says whether its result holds under the DKW band.

Result: not reproduced. The data set's labels give 200 mutant units (87 Chx10-Cre, 113 Pax6-Cre) and 122 control units (95 "WT (chx10 het)", 27 "WT (pax6 het)"), against 115 (103.5 to 126.5) and 143 (128.7 to 157.3). Units whose STA peak is more than 1.5 times the null's, a threshold chosen here, number 138 mutant and 113 control; more than 2 times, 103 and 107. Neither mutant count shown is inside its tolerance (103 is just below 103.5), but the mutant count falls from 138 to 103 between the two thresholds, so a threshold between them could put it inside; with the 20080702 frames as deposited the count above 1.5 is 126, inside it (cell 58). The control count cannot get there: no count of control units can exceed 122, below the lower bound. So the counts miss under any reading of "units with a flicker response" because of the control count. The 3 units of the Bax -/- retina are in neither group. The files give each unit's retina and label but not the region recorded in the Pax6-Cre retinas, so the per-retina table cannot be matched to the paper's peripheral subset.

# Example b(x) and a(t) (svd, reading A): in each group the cell with the largest STA peak ratio,
# the median cell of those above 2, and the median cell of those below 1.5.
def sta_of(retina, cell):
    rec = ret1.bar_recordings(by_name[retina], "A")[0]
    h, _ = ret1.sta(ret1.stimulus(rec, bits), ret1.counts(rec)[:, [cell]])
    return h[0], rec


A = cells[(cells.reading == "A") & cells.group.isin(GROUPS)]
picks = []
for g in GROUPS:
    x = A[A.group == g].sort_values("peak_ratio")
    strong, weak = x[x.peak_ratio > 2], x[x.peak_ratio < 1.5]
    picks += [("largest ratio", x.iloc[-1]), ("median of ratio > 2", strong.iloc[len(strong) // 2]), ("median of ratio < 1.5", weak.iloc[len(weak) // 2])]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 6, figsize=(16, 5))
rows = []
for k, (label, c) in enumerate(picks):
    h, rec = sta_of(c.retina, int(c.cell))
    b, a = ret1.separate(h, "svd")
    colour = "tab:red" if c.group == "mutant" else "black"
    axes[0, k].plot(np.arange(len(b)) * c.bar_um, b, color=colour)
    axes[0, k].set_title(f"{c.group}, {label}\n{c.retina} #{int(c.cell)}, ratio {c.peak_ratio:.2f}", fontsize=8)
    axes[0, k].set_xlabel("position (um)")
    axes[1, k].plot((np.arange(len(a)) + 0.5) * rec["frame"] * 1000, a, color=colour)
    axes[1, k].set_xlabel("time before spike (ms)")
    rows.append({"group": c.group, "pick": label, "retina": c.retina, "cell": int(c.cell), "peak_ratio": round(c.peak_ratio, 2),
                 "spikes": int(c.spikes_sta), "fwhm_um": round(c.fwhm_svd, 1), "ttp_ms": round(c.ttp_svd_frame * 1000, 1),
                 "surround_20": bool(c.surround_svd_20), "b_range": f"{b.min():.3g} to {b.max():.3g}", "a_range": f"{a.min():.3g} to {a.max():.3g}"})
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("b(x)"); axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("a(t)")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The outcome rests on one combination. The bands separate, with the mutant centres smaller, in 17 of the 18 combinations; only under reading B with the svd separation do the DKW bands overlap (medians 134 against 156 um, KS p = 0.004). With the 20080702 frames as deposited that combination separates too and all 18 separate (cell 56), which would give not reproduced. So the outcome turns on the frame correction of cell 16 and on one borderline DKW comparison. Under reading A, svd, the medians are 122 against 156 um (KS p below 1e-4). Much of the difference comes from mutant cells with weak STAs. Among cells whose STA peak is more than twice the null's (103 mutant, 107 control under reading A) the medians are 145 and 158 um (KS p = 0.19); the binomial and bootstrap bands separate only between 82 and 101 um, and the DKW bands overlap. Over the three readings in that subset, 13 of 18 combinations separate and 1 of the 6 DKW ones (reading C, peak). With the 16.6 um bars alone 16 of 18 separate, the svd DKW bands overlapping under readings A and B. The svd DKW bands also overlap with the Pax6-Cre mutants alone (reading A). In the example STAs, the two cells with ratios below 1.5 have centres of 63 and 38 um, narrower than the four cells with clear STAs (92 to 127 um). Under shuffled labels the binomial and bootstrap bands of this measure separate in 38 and 45% of shuffles, the DKW band in none.

s3-receptive-field-surrounds¶

Some control and mutant RGCs have receptive field surrounds of opposite sign to the centre, so lateral inhibition functions in mutant circuits.

A lobe of b(x) of opposite sign to the centre on both flanks, deeper than 10% (a) or 20% (b) of the centre peak. Reproduced when, under every combination of the two depths, the two separations and the three recording readings, at least one mutant and one control cell have one. The same rule applied to the null STA (spike counts shifted by half the recording) is shown as the reference for noise.

Result: reproduced by the criterion, but the test does not show surrounds. In all 12 readings at least one mutant and one control cell have a lobe of opposite sign on both flanks (reading A, svd, 20%: 90 of 200 mutant and 16 of 122 control cells). The same rule applied to null STAs (spike counts shifted by half the recording) is met by 194 to 198 of 200 mutant and 119 to 121 of 122 control cells, so noise alone meets it. Among cells with STA peak ratio above 2, at least 7 mutant and 4 control cells meet it at 20% in every reading. In the example STAs, both cells with ratios below 1.5 meet the rule at 20% and none of the four with clear STAs does. The result is no evidence for or against surrounds.

fig9e-slower-time-course¶

The time course of the light response is significantly slower in mutant retina, measured as the time to peak of the temporal integration function a(t).

Time to peak (s) of a(t), under both separations, both peak readings, the three band readings and the three recording readings. Reproduced when under every combination the bands separate with the mutant curve at longer times.

Range shown (ms): 38.0 to 491.8

Result: reproduced. In all 36 combinations the 95% bands separate with the mutant curve at longer times, and in none do they separate the other way. The mutant medians exceed the control medians by 16.7 to 33.3 ms (reading A, svd, frame: 125 against 108 ms; KS p at most 6e-10). Two mutant cells peak below 30 ms under reading A (STA peak ratios 0.86 and 1.05, no measurable receptive field), too few to separate the bands. The separation holds under the DKW band, which never separated under shuffled labels, and in every variant under reading A, including each Cre line alone and the Pax6-Cre heterozygous controls alone. Over all three readings (cell 56) all 36 combinations separate with the mutant curve later among cells with clear STAs, with 16.6 um bars alone and with the 20080702 frames as deposited. With the frames as deposited, 8 of them (binomial and bootstrap, peak separation, readings A and C) also hold 1 or 2 values where the bands separate the other way; the DKW bands never do.

Result: reproduced. In all 9 combinations the bands separate with the mutant curve at lower rates, under the DKW band too. Under reading A the mutant median is 3.82 Hz against 9.02 Hz for controls (ratio 0.42; 0.38 to 0.45 over the readings). By retina the mutant medians range from 1.9 to 15.9 Hz and the control medians from 3.8 to 23.6 Hz. Every variant gives a lower mutant median. With the Pax6-Cre mutants alone (ratio 0.68), and in the cells with clear STAs (0.66), the DKW bands overlap while the binomial and bootstrap bands still separate; those two bands separate in 38 and 39% of label shuffles for this measure. With the Pax6-Cre heterozygous controls alone (ratio 0.41) the DKW bands separate. Over the three readings (cell 56), the cells with clear STAs give 6 of 9 combinations separating and no DKW one, which the criterion would call blocked. The outcome holds on all units, which is how the claims file reads the groups, and depends on that reading. With the frames as deposited and with 16.6 um bars alone all 9 separate.

# LN fits whose theta is the first or last value of its search grid, by reading, group, fit and form,
# with those at the top (last value) and at the bottom (first value) counted apart.
rows = []
for rd in ret1.READINGS:
    d = cells[(cells.reading == rd) & cells.group.isin(GROUPS)]
    for f in ("frame", "binned"):
        for m in ("printed", "continuous"):
            for g in GROUPS:
                x = d[d.group == g]
                th = x[f"theta_{f}_{m}"]
                rows.append({"recording": rd, "fit": f, "form": m, "group": g, "fits": int(th.notna().sum()),
                             "at_grid_edge": int(x[f"theta_edge_{f}_{m}"].sum()), "at_top": int(x[f"theta_edge_top_{f}_{m}"].sum()),
                             "at_bottom": int(x[f"theta_edge_{f}_{m}"].sum() - x[f"theta_edge_top_{f}_{m}"].sum()),
                             "median_theta_at_top": round(float(th[x[f"theta_edge_top_{f}_{m}"].astype(bool)].median()), 2),
                             "median_theta": round(float(th.median()), 2),

Result: not reproduced. The paper finds the threshold unaltered. Here the bands separate in all 36 combinations, with mutant thresholds higher, under the DKW band too (reading A, frame fit: median 1.12 against 0.44 SD of the generator in the continuous form, 1.69 against 0.01 in the printed form). Part of this comes from mutant cells with weak STAs, whose generator predicts little of the rate. Among cells with clear STAs the medians are 0.86 against 0.41 (frame fit, continuous form, reading A); over the three readings in that subset 24 of 36 combinations separate (23 with mutant thresholds higher, 1 with values both ways) and no DKW one does (cell 56), which the criterion would call blocked. The outcome holds on all units, which is how the claims file reads the groups, and depends on that reading. With the frames as deposited and with 16.6 um bars alone all 36 separate. The binned fit in the printed form often stops at the last value of its theta grid, the split between its two highest bins of y (reading A: all 107 of the 107 mutant edge fits, of 200, median theta 1.86; 33 of the 39 control edge fits, of 122, with 6 at the first value). Why these fits reach the top is not shown here. Without the edge fits its medians are -0.03 and -0.03 (KS p = 0.21) and its DKW and bootstrap bands overlap, but that comparison removes most of the high mutant fits by construction, so it says nothing on whether the threshold is unaltered. The frame fit in the continuous form has 1 fit per group at an edge, both at the top, and separates under every band. With the Pax6-Cre heterozygous controls alone the DKW bands still separate, narrowly.

fig9h-gain-reduced¶

In the same Linear-Nonlinear model, the gain of mutant RGCs is reduced.

G (Hz per standard deviation of the generator) from the same fits, under the same readings. Reproduced when under every combination of the band, recording, fit and form readings the mutant curve lies at lower gains and the bands separate.

# The fits on synthetic cells of known parameters: generator y ~ N(0, 1) over 90,000 frames of
# 16.67 ms, Poisson spikes at B + G (y - theta) above theta (continuous form) or B + G y (printed),
# B = 2 Hz, G = 20 Hz per SD, theta from 0 to 1.5; 20 cells per setting.
rng = np.random.default_rng(9083)
rows = []
for true_form in ("continuous", "printed"):
    for theta in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5):
        fits = {(f, m): [] for f in ("frame", "binned") for m in ("printed", "continuous")}
        for _ in range(20):
            y = rng.standard_normal(90000)
            rate = 2.0 + np.where(y >= theta, 20.0 * (y - theta if true_form == "continuous" else y), 0.0)
            r = rng.poisson(np.clip(rate, 0, None) * 0.01667) / 0.01667
            for (f, m) in fits:
                fits[(f, m)].append(ret1.fit_ln(y, r, f, m))
        for (f, m), ps in fits.items():
            rows.append({"true_form": true_form, "true_theta": theta, "fit": f, "form": m,
                         "theta_median": round(float(np.median([p["theta"] for p in ps])), 2), "G_median": round(float(np.median([p["G"] for p in ps])), 1),
                         "at_edge": sum(p["edge"] for p in ps)})
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The readings of the nonlinearity's form disagree. With the printed form (B + G y above theta), the bands separate with mutant gains lower in all 18 combinations (reading A, frame fit: median 18.4 against 23.1 Hz per SD, ratio 0.80). With the continuous form (B + G (y - theta)), they overlap in 9 of 18, separate with mutant gains lower in 4 (reading B, binomial and bootstrap) and separate the other way in 5 (readings A and C). The medians are close (reading A, frame fit: 30.4 against 30.8, KS p = 0.76) and the DKW bands overlap in all 6 continuous-form combinations. Under reading B the separating values lie among the lowest gains (10 to 21 Hz per SD), and the first 8 to 10 of each lie among the 4 to 13 mutant gains below the lowest control gain, where the control band has zero width. Under reading A, frame fit, bootstrap, the one separating value (15.6) has 1 mutant against 6 control cells at or below it. The other separations the other way lie inside the distributions: under reading A, binned fit, at 41.46, with 165 of 200 mutant and 113 of 122 control cells at or below it; under reading C, frame fit, near 21.2, with 16 to 19 mutant against 23 to 25 control cells. Among cells with clear STAs neither form gives lower mutant gains under reading A (printed 23.1 against 23.4, continuous 33.1 against 31.0); over the three readings in that subset the printed form separates with mutant gains lower in 6 of 18 combinations (readings B and C) and the continuous form in 4, with 6 the other way and no DKW separation (cell 56), so the outcome there is blocked too. On synthetic cells that follow the continuous form, the printed-form fit returns a higher theta and a lower gain than the truth (true theta 0.5 and G 20: frame fit 0.75 and 13.4). So part of the printed-form gain reduction may mirror the higher mutant thresholds of fig9g-threshold-unaltered.

Every claim under the variants that bear on it, and all readings¶

Three variants are run here under all three recording readings (A, B, C), for every combination of each tested claim: the frames of the 20080702 bar recordings as deposited, the units whose STA peak is more than twice the null's (a threshold chosen here; the claims file uses all units), and the 16.6 um bar recordings alone. For each claim the table gives the combinations whose bands separate, by direction, and the DKW combinations that separate. The main analysis (frames corrected, all units) is computed again with the same seed for comparison; the claim sections above hold its tables.

In [32]:
CLAIM_COLS = {
    "fig9d-rf-size-similar": ["fwhm_svd", "fwhm_peak"],
    "fig9e-slower-time-course": [f"ttp_{s}_{p}" for s in ("svd", "peak") for p in ("frame", "parabolic")],
    "fig9f-lower-firing-rate": ["rate_hz"],
    "fig9g-threshold-unaltered": [f"theta_{f}_{m}" for f in ("frame", "binned") for m in ("printed", "continuous")],
    "fig9h-gain-reduced": [f"gain_{f}_{m}" for f in ("frame", "binned") for m in ("printed", "continuous")],
}
ALL_COLS = sum(CLAIM_COLS.values(), [])


def tally(res):
    """Per claim: combinations, those whose bands separate, by direction, and the DKW ones that separate."""
    out = []
    for claim, cols in CLAIM_COLS.items():
        r = res[res.measure.isin(cols)]
        s = r[r.separate]
        out.append({"claim": claim, "combinations": len(r), "separate": len(s),
                    "mutant_larger_only": int(((s.mutant_larger_pts > 0) & (s.mutant_smaller_pts == 0)).sum()),
                    "mutant_smaller_only": int(((s.mutant_smaller_pts > 0) & (s.mutant_larger_pts == 0)).sum()),
                    "both_ways": int(((s.mutant_larger_pts > 0) & (s.mutant_smaller_pts > 0)).sum()),
                    "dkw_separate": f"{int(s.ci.eq('dkw').sum())} of {int(r.ci.eq('dkw').sum())}"})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


def all_readings(select, seed):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    return pd.concat([judge(select(rd), ALL_COLS, rng).assign(recording=rd) for rd in ret1.READINGS], ignore_index=True)


def main_set(rd):
    return cells[(cells.reading == rd) & cells.group.isin(GROUPS)]


variant_sets = {
    "main analysis (frames corrected, all units)": main_set,
    "20080702 frames as deposited": lambda rd: cells[(cells.reading == f"{rd}, frames as deposited") & cells.group.isin(GROUPS)],
    "cells with STA peak ratio above 2": lambda rd: main_set(rd)[main_set(rd).peak_ratio > 2],
    "16.6 um bars only": lambda rd: main_set(rd)[main_set(rd).bar_um == 16.6],
}
variant_results = {k: all_readings(f, 910) for k, f in variant_sets.items()}
for k, res in variant_results.items():
    print(f"\n{k}:")
    print(tally(res).to_string(index=False))

# threshold (reading A). s3-receptive-field-surrounds: units meeting the rule, fewest over the 12 readings.
dep = cells[cells.reading.str.endswith("frames as deposited") & cells.group.isin(GROUPS)]

print(pd.DataFrame({"STA peak ratio above 1.5": dA[dA.peak_ratio > 1.5].groupby("group").size(),
                    "STA peak ratio above 2": dA[dA.peak_ratio > 2].groupby("group").size()}).to_string())
s3 = [{"recording": rd, "sep": sep, "depth": frac, "group": g, "meet": int(x[f"surround_{sep}_{frac}"].sum())}

      for x in [dep[(dep.reading == f"{rd}, frames as deposited") & (dep.group == g)]]]
print(pd.DataFrame(s3).groupby("group").meet.agg(["min", "max"]).to_string())

With the 20080702 frames as deposited, every claim gives the outcome of the main analysis except fig9d-rf-size-similar, whose 18 combinations then all separate (not reproduced); fig9e gains 8 combinations with values both ways, and the continuous-form gains of fig9h separate in 4 of 18 (all with mutant gains lower) in place of 9. With the 16.6 um bars alone the outcomes of fig9d to fig9h are those of the main analysis. Among the cells with clear STAs, fig9d-rf-size-similar and fig9h-gain-reduced stay blocked and fig9e-slower-time-course stays reproduced, but fig9f-lower-firing-rate and fig9g-threshold-unaltered would be blocked: no DKW band separates. The claims file reads the groups as all units, so the outcomes are given on all units. The same STA threshold gives 103 mutant and 107 control cells, nearest the paper's counts, but the paper does not say it selected cells this way. With the frames as deposited 126 mutant and 113 control units have STA peaks above 1.5 times the null's, and both groups have units meeting the surround rule in every reading.

Summary¶

Claim Outcome
15 histology claims (Figures 1 to 8, Supplementary Figure 1) Blocked: data missing
fig9a-response-variety, fig9c-on-off-index, fig9-rod-cone, fig9b-direction-selective Blocked: data missing
fig9-cell-counts: 115 mutant and 143 control cells Not reproduced (200 and 122)
fig9d-rf-size-similar: centre size similar Blocked: methods underspecified (17 of 18 combinations separate, mutant smaller)
s3-receptive-field-surrounds Reproduced by the criterion; the rule is met by noise
fig9e-slower-time-course Reproduced
fig9f-lower-firing-rate Reproduced
fig9g-threshold-unaltered Not reproduced (mutant higher)
fig9h-gain-reduced Blocked: methods underspecified (the forms of the nonlinearity disagree)

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's¶

  • The groups are the data set's labels. They hold 200 mutant and 122 control units, where the paper has 115 and 143. The control retinas are mostly labelled "WT (chx10 het)", a genotype the paper does not list among its controls. The files do not say which region of the Pax6-Cre retinas was recorded, so the mutant group cannot be restricted to the periphery as the paper's was. The Bax -/- retina is left out, as the paper did not use Bax mutants for Figure 9.
  • All units are used, as the claims file reads the legend's counts; the paper does not say whether it kept every unit. Many mutant units have weak or no receptive fields (STA peak below twice that of the null in 97 of 200 mutant units and 15 of 122 control units). Their noisy STAs give small centres, a high LN threshold and a low printed-form gain, and they carry much of the differences in Figure 9D, 9F, 9G and 9H. Among the units with STA peaks above twice the null's (103 mutant, 107 control under reading A), no DKW band separates for fig9f or fig9g, so on that subset both would be blocked; the outcomes of fig9f-lower-firing-rate and fig9g-threshold-unaltered depend on keeping every unit, as the claims file reads the groups. fig9e-slower-time-course holds on the subset, and fig9d and fig9h stay blocked.
  • The stimulus of the two 20080702 vertical-bar recordings is rebuilt with the frame of the other bar recordings (16.6718 ms), not the stated one, as the frame scan shows; a variant keeps the stated frames. Under all three readings, it changes the outcome of fig9d-rf-size-similar only (with the stated frames all 18 of its combinations separate, which would give not reproduced), so that outcome rests on the correction and on one borderline DKW comparison.
  • The paper does not say which bar recording is used. The claims file, after the question was answered, names three readings (A, B, C); all three were run. They agree on every outcome but that of fig9d-rf-size-similar, whose DKW band under reading B (svd) overlaps.
  • The 95% bands are built in the three ways the claims file names, as the paper does not say how its bands were made. Under shuffled labels the two pointwise bands separate in about 35% of comparisons and the DKW band in none, so the criteria's "overlap under every reading" is hard to meet for any pair of groups of this size. The LN fit and the separation of h follow the claims file's readings.
  • The mutant retinas include all 8.3 um bar recordings; all control retinas were stimulated with 16.6 um bars. With the 16.6 um recordings alone the outcomes of fig9d to fig9h are unchanged, though the svd DKW bands of fig9d then overlap under readings A and B, not only B.

What was found about the data set¶

  • It holds only the white-noise part of Figure 9: none of the histology of Figures 1 to 8, and no flashing spots, flashes, moving bars or gratings (Figure 9A to 9C).
  • Its unit counts (200 mutant, 122 control) and control genotypes differ from the paper's Figure 9 (115 and 143). The data set does not say how its units relate to the paper's.
  • In the 8 recordings of four retinas (20080628_R4 and R6, 20080702_R1 and R4), 82 of 86 spike trains run to 1440 s and then hold a second segment between 720 and 780 s, so they are not sorted. This is consistent with their last minute (1440 to 1500 s) stored with a 720 s offset in place of 1440 s.
  • The frame lengths stated for the vertical-bar recordings of 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4 (16.6691 and 16.6653 ms) are not those of the stimulus. Rebuilt with them, the bars of 20080702_R4 give no STA in any of its 12 units; rebuilt with 16.6718 ms, the frame of every other bar recording and half the checkerboard frame of the same retinas, 10 of the 12 have STA peaks above twice the null's.
  • 16 pairs of units share 70 to 100% of their spikes within 0.5 ms, most likely single neurons sorted twice.
  • The files do not give the age, the Pcdh-gamma allele, the recorded region of the Pax6-Cre retinas, or which units are ganglion cells of which type.
  • ran1.bin matches the RAN1 generator of ran1.m with seed -10000, read least significant bit first, and the description's table of retinas, cells and labels matches the files.
